patterns.usage_note: The plain te-form link between clauses: で after nouns and な-adjectives (風邪[かぜ]で) and wherever the te-form is voiced (む/ぶ/ぬ and ぐ godan verbs: 呼[よ]んで, 泳[およ]いで), て elsewhere, くて for i-adjectives. It leaves the relation between the clauses to context, so it reads as sequence, simultaneous description, or loose cause depending on content. On the causal reading the main clause is typically a statement of fact rather than a command or request. Where the noun + で is doing nothing but stringing two descriptions of the same topic together (兄は医者で、弟は教師だ), that is the copula's linking form in the ダ類 family; this entry is the connective that makes the second clause follow from the first.

examples.ruby: 風邪[かぜ]で三日[みっか]も学校[がっこう]を休[やす]みました。
examples.english: A cold kept me out of school for three whole days.

examples.ruby: 友達[ともだち]を呼[よ]んで一緒[いっしょ]に晩[ばん]ご飯[はん]を作[つく]った。
examples.english: I invited a friend over and we made dinner together.

examples.ruby: 荷物[にもつ]が重[おも]くて一人[ひとり]では持[も]てなかった。
examples.english: The luggage was so heavy I couldn't carry it alone.
